title: Verifiable blind probabilistic error cancellation
authors: Bo Yang, Elham Kashefi, Harold Ollivier
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is an essential tool for mitigating hardware noise without incurring space overhead. Yet, its reliability depends on modeling, calibration, and implementation, leaving end-to-end security on untrusted quantum hardware unresolved. We address this problem by introducing verifiable blind probabilistic error cancellation (VBPEC), the first secure verification protocol against a fully malicious adversary that integrates QEM. VBPEC brings probabilistic error cancellation (PEC), a widely studied QEM technique, within the scope of composable security by formalizing delegated mitigation as a cryptographic resource in the abstract cryptography framework. The protocol performs PEC with perfect blindness and an exponentially small security error. VBPEC retains the absence of quantum-space overhead from recent statistically-secure verified quantum computation protocols and from PEC. The only overhead takes the form of additional repetitions due to the QEM procedure. To achieve this, we extend trap-based verification from deterministic pass/fail checks to statistical tests that benefit from QEM and develop a new proof technique that integrates the corresponding additional deviation sources. Rather than merely tolerating honest noise below a fixed threshold, VBPEC actively cancels it, enabling correctly mitigated estimates to be accepted with high probability without compromising security. Our framework thus establishes an essential route towards secure, reliable, and practical delegated quantum computation on near-future quantum hardware: VBPEC fundamentally improves the practicality of verification.
summary: This paper presents Verifiable Blind Probabilistic Error Cancellation (VBPEC), a novel protocol that secures Quantum Error Mitigation (QEM) when running computations on untrusted quantum hardware. It achieves this by formally integrating PEC into composable security, allowing the active cancellation of noise rather than just tolerating it. This establishes a crucial pathway toward reliable and practical delegated quantum computation.
main_problem: The core problem is establishing end-to-end security guarantees for quantum computations performed on untrusted, noisy hardware by integrating Quantum Error Mitigation (QEM) into verifiable protocols.
main_result: The paper introduces Verifiable Blind Probabilistic Error Cancellation (VBPEC), the first secure protocol to integrate PEC within a composable security framework, providing cryptographic reliability for QEM.
method: It extends trap-based verification from deterministic checks to statistical tests that actively cancel noise rather than merely tolerating it, formalizing delegated mitigation as a cryptographic resource.
model_or_system: The work addresses the abstract model of quantum computation delegated to an untrusted server. The underlying physical processes involve observable estimation ($	ext{Tr}[ho O]$) on near-future quantum hardware.

important_parameters: Estimation error $\epsilon$ and confidence level $\delta$; the number of samples $N_c$.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes access to a fully malicious adversary model, requiring cryptographic guarantees for noise cancellation.

paper_structure: The paper builds from standard observable estimation theory to Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC), extends this to a blind setting (BDPEC), and culminates in the universal framework (VBPEC) that provides cryptographic security guarantees for QEM.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical gap between theoretical quantum algorithms and noisy, untrusted hardware by providing rigorous cryptographic verification for error mitigation techniques.
